lesson.subject: english
lesson.title: Sentences and Grammar
lesson.summary: Describing words, plurals, joining sentences with and, but and because, the three kinds of sentence, capital letters and commas, and -ed and -ing.
learning_objectives: Use describing words to say more about a thing
Make plurals with s and es
Join ideas with and, but and because
Use capital letters for names and commas in lists

standards.text: Use expanded noun phrases, co-ordination (and, but) and subordination (because), and the correct sentence punctuation

success_criteria: I can find a describing word in a sentence
I can join two ideas with and, but or because
I can tell a statement, a question and an exclamation
I can use capital letters and commas in a list
lesson.real_life: Writing a message to a friend, a shopping list and a postcard.

blocks.markdown:
Today's big question: how can we make our sentences clear and exciting?

We will learn to describe, join and punctuate.
blocks.say: Welcome back, word explorer! Today we have a big question. How can we make our sentences exciting and clear, so everyone enjoys reading them? We will learn how to describe things, join ideas, use the right marks, and talk about now and before. By the end, you will be a sentence builder. Let's go!

blocks.alt: Sentence builders use words and marks to make writing clear.
blocks.caption: Sentence builders use words and marks to make writing clear.

terms.meaning: A group of words that makes sense on its own.

blocks.markdown:
A **describing word** tells us more about a thing.

A big dog. A small dog. Big and small describe the dog.
blocks.say: Look at these two dogs. Both of them are dogs. But they are not the same! One is big and one is small. Big and small are describing words. A describing word tells us more about a thing. It helps us see the picture in our head. A big dog. A small dog. A fluffy dog. Let's watch the describing words appear.

scenes.caption: A dog.
scenes.say: Here is a dog. Just a dog. We cannot tell much about it yet.

scenes.caption: A big dog.
scenes.say: Now there are two dogs. This one is big. Big tells us how large the dog is.

scenes.caption: A big dog and a small dog.
scenes.say: And this one is small. Small is a describing word too. Big and small tell us what each dog is like.

question.prompt: Which is the describing word in: the tall tree?
question.hint: Which word tells us more about the tree?
question.explanation: Tall tells us what the tree is like.

question.hint: Can you say a soft blanket?
question.explanation: Soft tells us how a thing feels, so it is a describing word.

blocks.markdown:
**Plural** means more than one.

Most words add s: one cat, two cats.

Words ending in s, x, sh or ch add es: one box, two boxes.
blocks.say: Now let's count. One cat. Two cats. When there is more than one, we say the word is plural. Most words just need an s on the end. One cat, two cats. One book, two books. But some words need es instead. A box becomes boxes. A bus becomes buses. A dish becomes dishes. Say it out loud and you can hear the extra bit.

scenes.caption: One cat.
scenes.say: One cat. Just one.

scenes.caption: Two cats. Add s.
scenes.say: Now there are two. We add an s. Two cats.

scenes.caption: One box.
scenes.say: One box.

scenes.caption: Two boxes. Add es.
scenes.say: Box ends in x. So we do not add just s. We add es. Two boxes. You can hear the extra part: box-es.

question.hint: Bus ends in s, so add es.
question.explanation: Words ending in s add es: bus, buses.

question.prompt: Which word means more than one?
question.explanation: Dogs has an s, so it means more than one.

blocks.markdown:
A **verb** is a doing word: jump, kick, walk.

Add -ing for now: I am jumping.

Add -ed for before: Yesterday I jumped.
blocks.say: Doing words tell us what someone does. Jump, kick, walk. We can change the ending to say when it happens. Add ing when it is happening now. I am jumping. Add ed when it already happened. Yesterday I jumped. Watch the girl jump, and see how the word changes.

scenes.caption: Jump.
scenes.say: Jump. This is the doing word, jump.

scenes.caption: I am jumping. Add -ing.
scenes.say: Now she is in the air. Right now, she is jumping. We add ing for now.

scenes.caption: Yesterday I jumped. Add -ed.
scenes.say: And now she is back on the ground. Before, she jumped. We add ed for something that is finished.

question.explanation: Kicking with am means it is happening now.
Opened ends in -ed, so it already happened.

points: A describing word tells us more about a thing
Plural means more than one: cats, boxes
blocks.say: Let us remember. A describing word tells us more about a thing. A plural means more than one. Add s, or es for words like box and bus. And add ing for now, or ed for before.

sub_lessons.title: Joining with and, but and because

blocks.markdown:
**And** adds more: I have a hat and a scarf.

**But** shows something different: I like apples but not pears.

**Because** tells us why: I took my umbrella because it was raining.
blocks.say: Short sentences are fine. But joining them makes our writing sound smooth. Today we have three joining words. And, but, and because. And adds more. I have a hat and a scarf. But shows something different. I like apples but I do not like pears. Because tells us why. I took my umbrella because it was raining. Let's see each one working.

scenes.caption: I have a hat and a scarf.
scenes.say: And adds one more thing. A hat and a scarf. We have two things together.

scenes.caption: I like apples but not pears.
scenes.say: But shows something different. I like apples. But I do not like pears. The two ideas pull in different ways.

scenes.caption: I took my umbrella because it was raining.
scenes.say: Because tells us why. I took my umbrella. Why? Because it was raining!

question.prompt: Pick the best word: I like tea ___ I do not like coffee.
question.explanation: Liking tea and not liking coffee are different, so we use but.

question.prompt: Pick the best word: We stayed inside ___ it was raining.
question.explanation: The rain is the reason we stayed in, so we use because.

blocks.title: Join the sentences
materials: A grown-up to read with you
instructions: Finish this sentence three ways: I like ...
Use and. For example: I like cake and ice cream.
Use but. For example: I like cake but I do not like jelly.
Use because. For example: I like cake because it is sweet.
blocks.say: Now it is your turn to build. Say a sentence out loud with and. Then one with but. Then one with because. Saying them first makes writing them much easier. A grown-up can help you write them down.

blocks.say: Here is a question to think about. Can you finish this one: I was happy because ...? Have a think, then tap to see one idea.
Let us remember. And adds more. But shows something different. Because tells us why.

blocks.markdown:
A **statement** tells us something and ends with a full stop.

A **question** asks something and ends with a question mark.

An **exclamation** shows a big feeling and ends with an exclamation mark.
blocks.say: Sentences do different jobs! A statement tells us something. The sun is hot. It ends with a full stop. A question asks something. Is the sun hot? It ends with a question mark. An exclamation shows a big feeling. The sun is so hot! It ends with an exclamation mark. Look at the marks. They are like little signs telling us what kind of sentence it is.

scenes.caption: The sun is hot.
scenes.say: A statement. The sun is hot. It tells us a fact. It stops with a full stop.

scenes.caption: Is the sun hot?
scenes.say: A question. Is the sun hot? It asks us something, so it ends with a question mark.

scenes.caption: The sun is so hot!
scenes.say: An exclamation. The sun is so hot! It shows a big feeling, so it ends with an exclamation mark.

question.explanation: A question ends with a question mark.
Where is my bag? asks something, so it is a question.

blocks.markdown:
Names of people, places and days start with a **capital letter**: Zainab, Lahore, Monday.

Every sentence starts with a capital letter too.
blocks.say: Some words are so special they get a big letter at the start. A capital letter. Names of people get one. Zainab. Names of places get one. Lahore. And so do days of the week. Monday. We call these special names proper nouns. Also, every sentence starts with a capital letter. Watch the big letters grow.

scenes.caption: zainab needs a capital.
scenes.say: A girl called zainab. Hold on, that does not look right. A name needs a big letter at the start.

scenes.caption: Zainab, Lahore and Monday.
scenes.say: There it is! Zainab, with a capital Z. Names of places get a capital too, like Lahore. And days, like Monday.

blocks.markdown:
A **comma** keeps things in a list apart.

I packed an apple, a banana and a sandwich.
blocks.say: When we write a list of things, we use a comma between them. A comma is a little tail that tells us to take a tiny pause. I packed an apple, a banana and a sandwich. There is a comma after apple. Then and joins the last two. We do not need a comma before and.

scenes.caption: An apple, a banana and a sandwich.
scenes.say: Here are three things in the lunch box. An apple, a banana and a sandwich.

scenes.caption: apple, banana and sandwich
scenes.say: We put a comma after apple, a tiny pause. And joins the last two. Say it out loud: apple, banana and sandwich.
